clue.text: Wet swan seen on reservoir

indicators.note: in an across answer one piece seen on another is written after it

parts.note: a dam is a body of water held back, a reservoir
a pen is a female swan

explanation.surface: A swan is spotted swimming on a reservoir, getting wet.
explanation.definitionFit: To moisten something slightly is to make it wet.

clue.text: Sort out import price he'd fiddled

indicators.note: fiddled figures have been tampered with and rearranged, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone untangles the bill for imported goods whose price a trader cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddled' rearranges PRICEHED. 'import' looks like trade goods but here means meaning: to sort out the import of something is to work out what it says.
explanation.definitionFit: Working out the meaning of a message is decoding it, making sense of its significance.

clue.text: Island bird grabbing some worm in, or caterpillar

indicators.note: the definition grabs some of the following words, a run of letters hidden inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A bird on an island snatches a worm or a caterpillar.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition ran on to 'grabbing', but that word belongs with 'some' as the hidden-word signal; 'Island bird' alone is the definition, with both senses fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: The Balearic island has given its name to a breed of domestic chicken, so the word is both a place and a fowl.

clue.text: Lights so ideal for tree?

parts.note: traffic lights would be ideal for a driver if they always showed go; that wish names a tree that keeps its leaves all year

explanation.surface: A question about which lights best suit a tree, like decorations at Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree that keeps its foliage through every season is called this, as opposed to deciduous.

clue.text: Tissue that can make nose uncomfortable

definitions.text: Tissue that can make nose uncomfortable

parts.words: Tissue that can make nose uncomfortable
parts.note: reads like a rough paper handkerchief, but means glandular growth at the back of the nasal passage that blocks breathing

explanation.surface: A cheap paper hanky leaves a sore nose.
explanation.definitionFit: These are lymph tissue masses behind the nasal cavity which, when swollen, obstruct the nose.

clue.text: Girl's date is a flop

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, a short form of Diana, plus the possessive S
a date is an arranged meeting, an appointment

explanation.surface: A girl's date with someone turns out to be a failure.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that fails to meet hopes, a let-down, is a flop.

clue.text: One Pole or another East European type

parts.note: N stands for north, one of the earth's poles
taken as written
another pole is S for south

explanation.surface: Someone sizes up a Polish person, or another kind of East European.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a nationality, but it is a magnetic or geographic pole, N or S.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scandinavian of the Viking age, especially Norwegian, is a kind of European.

clue.text: Get ready to work where animal's housed

definitions.meaning: to put equipment in place ready for use
an animal kept in a stable stall is in its stall, read as two words

explanation.surface: A stable hand gets set for the day's work where the horse is kept.
explanation.definitionFit: Fitting a machine so it works is setting it up; the same letters split give the phrase for being kept in a stable compartment.

clue.text: Tender as Ophelia was to Laertes

definitions.meaning: a tender is a carer, and in Britain a senior hospital nurse is given this title
in Hamlet Ophelia and Laertes are siblings, children of Polonius

explanation.surface: Ophelia is gentle and caring towards her brother Laertes in Shakespeare's play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender' looks like an adjective (gentle) but is a noun, one who tends: a British ward nurse is called by this title.
explanation.definitionFit: A nurse who tends patients, and a female sibling, share this one word.

clue.text: Reason for entering huge wave that's off Irish coast

parts.note: huge means giant

indicators.note: the reason word is written entering, inside, the wave word

parts.note: to sway is to wave to and fro
a cause is a reason

explanation.surface: Someone explains why a huge wave is breaking off the coast of Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for entering' puts CAUSE inside SWAY to make SCAUSEWAY. The definition is loose: the basalt columns run out into the sea from the County Antrim shore in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous field of basalt columns stands at the sea's edge in Northern Ireland, stretching into the water.

clue.text: Recognise movement in mass

indicators.note: movement in the letters of the word means they are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone spots a movement in a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: This rare word means a disorderly collection or heap, a mass of things.

clue.text: In more ways than one, they may make a fine spray

definitions.text: In more ways than one, they may make a fine spray

parts.words: In more ways than one, they may make a fine spray
parts.note: a bunch of these flowers makes a lovely spray, and the perforated nozzle of a watering can shares their name and sprays fine water

explanation.surface: Something produces a pleasing fine spray, in more than one sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Flowers gathered into a bouquet form a spray, and the sprinkler head of a watering can is called by the same word.

clue.text: Quiet part of Spain is ideal

parts.note: P is piano, the musical term for quiet
Aragon is a region of north-east Spain

explanation.surface: A peaceful region of Spain is the perfect place.
explanation.definitionFit: A model of excellence, a perfect example, is an ideal.

clue.text: Cardinal, say, about to contribute to the collection

indicators.note: the word for about is put into the collection, as a coin dropped in the plate

parts.note: the plate is passed round church for the collection
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A cardinal is about to put money in the church collection.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardinal is one example of a senior churchman such as a bishop or archbishop.

clue.text: Make exultant finalising previous answer

indicators.note: finalising means keeping only the final part of that word, dropping its opening letters

parts.note: refers to the answer of the clue before, 13 across

explanation.surface: A quiz host is overjoyed at finishing off the last answer.
explanation.walkthrough: The previous clue's answer is PRELATE; 'finalising' keeps only its final five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To fill someone with joy and pride is to make them exultant.

clue.text: Fast road into airport — on the way in boisterous fashion

indicators.note: in an across answer the airport piece placed on the street piece follows it

parts.note: St is street, a way

indicators.note: the road is put into the airport's name

parts.note: Orly is a Paris airport
MI is the M1, Britain's first motorway

explanation.surface: A motorway leads to an airport, with traffic on the way moving wildly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' puts MI inside ORLY to make ORMILY, which follows ST. 'Fast' tempts as the definition but belongs to the motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting wildly and noisily, like a tempest, is behaving boisterously.

clue.text: Declaration of intent has obvious omission, lacking sense of purpose

parts.note: manifest means obvious

indicators.note: lacking means the word omission is written without the word for sense of purpose

parts.note: the word omission is taken as written before cutting
a mission is a sense of purpose, a calling

explanation.surface: A party's declared programme has a glaring gap and lacks direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' takes MISSION out of OMISSION, leaving O, which follows MANIFEST.
explanation.definitionFit: A published statement of a party's aims and policies is a declaration of intent.

clue.text: Newsman in army personnel carrier

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, British army personnel
a porter carries luggage

explanation.surface: A journalist rides in an armoured troop carrier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'army personnel carrier' reads as one military vehicle; split it into the Royal Engineers and a luggage carrier.
explanation.definitionFit: A journalist who gathers and writes news is a newsman.

clue.text: Start to grow a popular fruit

parts.note: to plant a seed is to start it growing
in means fashionable, popular

explanation.surface: Gardening advice: begin growing a well-liked fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A starchy banana-like fruit cooked as a vegetable in the tropics.

clue.text: Berth set up in accommodation for members

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: to berth a ship is to moor it
to gel is to set, as a jelly does

explanation.surface: A bunk is installed in quarters for club members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns MOORGEL round. 'members' are limbs, here legs, not club members.
explanation.definitionFit: Space for one's legs in a seat is room for limbs, and limbs are members.

clue.text: Half-heartedly try to influence peer

indicators.note: half of the doubled letters at the heart of the word is dropped

parts.note: to nobble is to try to sway someone improperly, as by bribery

explanation.surface: A lobbyist makes a feeble attempt to sway a member of the Lords.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-heartedly' removes one of the two Bs at the middle of NOBBLE. A peer is a member of Britain's House of Lords.
explanation.definitionFit: A lord or other titled aristocrat is a peer of the realm.

clue.text: It helps one keep up one's reading

definitions.text: It helps one keep up one's reading

parts.words: It helps one keep up one's reading
parts.note: sounds like a study aid, but means a prop that holds a row of volumes upright on a shelf

explanation.surface: Something helps you stay on top of your reading list.
explanation.definitionFit: A weighted support at the end of a row of volumes keeps them standing.

clue.text: Professional man beginning to panic over crime

indicators.note: in a down answer, over means the first piece sits above the next
beginning to takes just the first letter of the word panic

parts.note: arson is the crime of fire-raising

explanation.surface: A professional starts to panic about a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman is a member of one of the traditional learned professions.

clue.text: A new attempt by artists to show various animals

parts.note: a go is an attempt
RAs are Royal Academicians, artists

explanation.surface: Painters make a fresh attempt at depicting a range of animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Goats, rabbits and cats of this long-haired kind are several types of animal.

clue.text: Quick attack captures pawn

indicators.note: captures means the attack word holds the pawn letter inside it

parts.note: a raid is an attack
P is the chess notation for a pawn

explanation.surface: In chess, a fast attack takes a pawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Fast, swift and speedy all mean quick.

clue.text: Gangster to be fearful of? So am I

indicators.note: fearful letters are agitated and jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Asked if a gangster is someone to fear, the speaker agrees: they are frightened too.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Sicilian-American crime syndicate is a gangster.

clue.text: Sudden raid to bring back prisoners netting nothing

indicators.note: netting means the reversed word catches the letter for nothing inside it
to bring back means the prisoners word is turned round

parts.note: POWs are prisoners of war
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A surprise raid aims to bring prisoners home but catches nobody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to bring back' turns POWS into SWOP, and 'netting' puts O inside that.
explanation.definitionFit: A swift sudden descent or attack, as by a bird of prey, is a sudden raid.

clue.text: Cried by turns, feeling loss of parting perhaps

indicators.note: by means set beside, the one piece next to the other

parts.note: winds means turns, as a road does
wept means cried

explanation.surface: Someone sobbed now and again, grieving a farewell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parting' looks like a farewell but is the line in combed hair, which a gale messes up.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair blown about by a gale has lost its neat combed line.

clue.text: Feasts damn easy to organise

indicators.note: to organise these letters is to put them into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Throwing feasts is dashed easy to arrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Saints' days celebrated by those named after the saint are festivals.

clue.text: Admiration produced by puzzle

definitions.meaning: awe and amazement, an admiring feeling
as a verb, to puzzle over something is to ponder it

explanation.surface: A puzzle earns admiration.
explanation.definitionFit: Amazement felt at something marvellous, and pondering in doubt, are both expressed by one word.
